# Moodle CLI 0.9.6

`moodle dl` now saves whole sections and assignment files and lets you browse a unit at the terminal. This release also closes every place where the CLI could take an irreversible step without telling you first, starting with `moodle submit` handing an assignment in for grading when it had been asked only to save a draft.

## Highlights

- **`moodle submit` without `--final` never submits for grading.** If an assignment has no draft stage, or its pages do not show whether it has one, the command refuses before uploading anything.
- **`moodle dl` downloads what the course page offers:** one activity, a whole section including its child sections, an assignment's attached files, or a `pluginfile.php` link. At a terminal it browses unit → section → item.
- **Quizzes that move forward only are safe to step through.** The CLI never opens the next page without asking you first, because opening it locks the current page for good.
- **`quiz start` tells you the time limit and attempts left** before the timer starts.
- **`mcp revoke` asks first**, and client config files are written atomically.

## `moodle submit` no longer submits a draft for grading

Some assignments have no draft stage: in Moodle, saving the files is itself the submission for grading, and that cannot be undone. Earlier versions knew this could happen and saved anyway, so `moodle submit ID files --accept-statement --yes` without `--final` handed the work in.

Moodle never states the setting, so the CLI works it out from the pages:
- The edit form carries the submission statement only when there is no draft stage.
- A "Submit assignment" button appears only when there is one.
- A submission that is already submitted but can still be edited means there is none.

Without `--final`, a save goes ahead only when Moodle shows a draft stage. "No draft stage" and "can't tell" are both refused before anything is uploaded. If Moodle submits on save anyway, the command fails loudly instead of reporting a draft. The plan and receipt carry `draft_stage`, and the confirmation says plainly whether saving submits.

Two more checks:
- `--replace` with no files is refused rather than emptying the submission.
- In a group submission the plan names the group, because its files are shared: an upload or `--replace` changes every member's submission. When every member has to submit, the receipt lists who Moodle is still `awaiting` instead of reporting a failure.

## Download sections, assignment files and links

`moodle download` (alias `dl`) accepts an activity, a section (`moodle dl "UNIT week 5"` or a section URL) or a single `pluginfile.php` link. A section download includes the child sections the page shows inside it. An assignment download saves its attached files, such as the brief and datasets.

With no argument at a terminal, it walks unit → section → item the way the course page does: type to filter, Escape to go back a step. Short forms such as `a2` or `w7` match. Repeated section names are shown with their parent, as in `Week 5 › Own time`.

Files already on disk are skipped, so rerunning after Ctrl+C or a dropped connection fetches only what is missing; `--force` downloads everything again. The same document linked twice is saved once, and two different files with one name get a ` (2)` suffix. Ctrl+C stops at once and leaves no partial files, and a file without a name is skipped instead of failing the whole batch. `--dry-run` writes nothing. The run ends with a one-line receipt.

A slow download is no longer cut off at 30 seconds. Instead, a connection that sends nothing for a while times out, and each redirect gets its own limit.

## Quizzes

A quiz set to sequential navigation locks each page once you open the next one. `moodle quiz` now reads that setting from the attempt page and handles it:
- `quiz show --page` refuses a locked page or a skip, and asks before opening the next page.
- `quiz answer` refuses questions that are not on the current page.
- The next-step hints never suggest going back.

Before `quiz start` asks for confirmation, it says whether it will continue an attempt or start a new one. It also shows the attempt number and how many are allowed, the grading method, and the time limit: the timer starts at once and does not pause. `--dry-run` shows the same plan without starting anything.

## Units, due dates and tables

- Sections nest under the parents the site reports, and the MCP `unit` tool shows week sections with their children.
- A current section is shown only when the site marks one; no more guesses.
- Due dates count calendar days, so something due in 90 minutes reads "today", not "tomorrow". Quiz openings are labelled as openings.
- `moodle UNIT "assignment 2"` finds the assignment instead of a section, and an exact item name wins over a partial match.
- Unit dates are shown in the site's timezone.
- `moodle grades` shows due dates in their own column.
- Tables use the full terminal width for long names.
- The MCP `file` tool follows shortcut activities and fetches any activity that holds a single file.

## MCP deployment safety

- **`moodle mcp revoke` and `revoke --all` ask first.** Scripts pass `--yes`, and `--dry-run` shows what would be revoked.
- **The `--rotate-token` help text now says what really happens:** the old token and every connected OAuth client, including claude.ai, stop working at once. It used to promise an overlap window that did not exist.
- **Client config files, `config.yaml` and the renewal job are written atomically,** so a crash or full disk cannot leave a half-written file. A symlinked config keeps its link.
- **A failed client registration no longer overwrites a file the client itself has changed since.** Claude Code rewrites `~/.claude.json` constantly, so restoring the old copy could throw away its changes.
- **One unreadable client config no longer blocks the rest.** Every client is tried, and the ones that failed are named together.

## Upgrade

```bash
npm install -g moodle-cli@0.9.6
```

Or:

```bash
moodle update
```

`moodle update` also redeploys a managed MCP Worker, which is needed for its `unit` and `file` changes. No configuration or cache format changes.
